title: One trick short of your target

feedback.title: Take the trick you still need
feedback.summary: You are below target: 3 taken, 4 estimated. The king beats the queen and takes your fourth trick. After that, further tricks would be unwanted.
points: You act last after East, North and West. Everyone has played Hearts, so no trump can beat your king in this trick.
Both Hearts are legal; the Club and Diamond are locked by follow-suit.
Taking this known opportunity is the reviewed preference. It does not guarantee finishing on four: the remaining three tricks are unresolved.

feedback.title: Still short, with a safe trick passed up
feedback.summary: The three loses to the queen, leaving you below target at 3 of 4. You pass up a certain needed trick and rely on a later opportunity.
points: Saving the king may work later, but the unseen cards and future leads are unknown.
Avoiding a trick is not automatically good: you have not reached your estimate yet.

author_notes: EC-043 contrast pair with _002: identical hand and current trick, different visible taken counts. No hidden-card or final-round guarantee. No auction context is needed for this decision.
